title: The Furuta nineteen ninety eight paper

segs.text: Section twenty two. The Furuta nineteen ninety eight discussion, C Y P two C nineteen, omeprazole, and H pylori cure. Furuta and colleagues compared H pylori cure rates by C Y P two C nineteen genotype. She used the paper to make students work from the paper's old allele labels to star nomenclature, and from genotype to enzyme activity. She said, You guys have to be able to drill down from your phenotype of your patient to the molecular structure of the D N A and know what is star two? What is star three? Why is that enzyme not active in this person?

The study enrolled sixty two Japanese patients, mostly middle aged men, with a gastric or duodenal ulcer and H pylori infection. They took omeprazole twenty milligrams for eight weeks for a gastric ulcer or six weeks for a duodenal ulcer, plus amoxicillin five hundred milligrams four times a day for two weeks. That is one P P I, a proton pump inhibitor, with one antibiotic. In the United States, H pylori is usually treated with triple therapy, a P P I with two antibiotics. The paper calls the enzyme S mephenytoin four prime hydroxylase, an older name for C Y P two C nineteen.

In star nomenclature, wild type is star one, m one is star two, and m two is star three. Group one, star one star one, has normal activity and a cure rate of twenty eight point six percent. Group two carries one star one allele with star two or star three. It still makes some functional enzyme, and the cure rate was sixty percent. Group three carries two of the variant alleles, has no activity, and every patient was cured, one hundred percent. Star two and star three are S N Ps that create a premature stop codon, so the protein is too short to work. No patient was star three star three. Such a patient would simply belong in group three, so the gap only reflects who was recruited.

The discussion section explains why poor metabolizers were cured more often. Omeprazole stays high, so stomach p H stays higher. Amoxicillin is unstable at low p H, so it is more stable at the higher p H. Omeprazole also helps get amoxicillin into the gastric juice, where H pylori is. She said group three had the highest A U C, but the paper did not measure plasma omeprazole levels. It cites relative A U Cs of one to three point seven to twenty from earlier work. This paper used omeprazole with amoxicillin. Lansoprazole was a different figure, from two thousand four.

Can the result be applied in the United States? She said, Not on the face of it. Star two and star three are relatively frequent in Japanese people. The paper gives the poor metabolizer genotype as eighteen to twenty three percent in Japanese persons, versus three to five percent in white U S or European populations. With genotyping, the same response is expected and only the group sizes differ, so fewer antibiotics might be possible for the right genotypes.
